title: Lesson 4. Box model — an element is a box
description: content, padding, border, margin and box-sizing: border-box

learn.intro: Hi! Lesson 4 — the **Box model**. Every element on a page is a box. Let's unpack it like a parcel, layer by layer. Let's go!

slides.text: Every element on a page is a **box**. A heading is a box, text is a box, a button is a box too.

Imagine a parcel. It has 4 parts:
🎁 the item itself — **content** (text or an image)
🧻 the wrapping around the item — **padding** (empty space inside)
📦 the cardboard of the box — **border** (the frame)
↔️ the distance to other boxes — **margin** (empty space outside)
**Content** is what's inside the tag. Here the content is the word «Hello!»:
Remember the order from inside out: content → padding → border → margin.

check.prompt: Put the box layers in order from inside out
A button on a page is a box too.

slides.text: **Padding** is the empty space **inside**, between the text and the frame. An item is wrapped in foam so it doesn't touch the walls of the box. Padding moves the text away from the edge the same way.
The text moves 20px in from the edge, and the blue background gets bigger:
Padding is INSIDE. The background color also covers the padding.

options: Between the text and the frame
check.explain: padding is the empty space inside the box.

sections.title: Border — the cardboard of the box

slides.text: **Border** is the edge of the box, its frame. It sits outside the padding.

`border: 2px solid black;` — three words:
`2px` — frame thickness
`solid` — style: a solid line (`dashed` — a dashed line)
`black` — frame color
The border goes around the padding, like cardboard around the item's wrapping.

check.prompt: Match the part of border: 2px solid black and its meaning

slides.text: **Margin** is the empty space **outside**: the distance from the box to other boxes. In a warehouse boxes aren't pressed together — space is left between them.
30px of empty space appears between box 1 and box 2:
`margin-top` — above, `margin-bottom` — below, `margin-left` — on the left, `margin-right` — on the right, `margin` — on all sides at once.
Margin is OUTSIDE. The background color doesn't cover the margin, it's always transparent.

check.prompt: The box's background also colors the margin.
check.explain: margin is always transparent; the background covers only content and padding.

check.prompt: Which property adds space only on the left?
check.explain: margin-left is the outer space on the left.

slides.text:
We give a box `width: 200px`, then add `padding: 20px`. How wide is it? Many say 200px, but the browser counts differently:
20px + 200px + 20px = **240px**. The page breaks.
The fix goes in the very first line of the CSS file:
Now with `width: 200px` the box stays 200px: padding and border fit inside. To check: **F12 → Elements → Computed** — it shows the real size.
In every project the first line of CSS is * { box-sizing: border-box; }. Always!

check.prompt: Without box-sizing: width: 200px + padding: 20px. How wide is the box in px? (number only)
Where can you check the real size of a box?
check.explain: The Computed tab shows the real sizes.

slides.text: Make 3 identical boxes: give the first `padding: 30px`, the second `border: 5px solid red`, the third `margin: 40px`. Look at how they differ. Then add `* { box-sizing: border-box; }` at the top of the CSS and compare again.

Homework: 3 product cards in one row with equal spacing. Each has a name, a price and a button. Use padding, border and margin, and put `* { box-sizing: border-box; }` at the top of the CSS. Hint: `.card { display: inline-block; width: 250px; }`.

check.prompt: What do you use to move the cards apart?
check.explain: The distance between boxes is the margin.
